claims.wording: F_dual(x) = x^2/2 - (x - ln(1+x)) is the unique Pade[1/1] AQUAL potential and decomposes into H = x^2/2 and L_corr = x - ln(1+x).
assumptions: Uniqueness holds WITHIN the two-parameter Pade[1/1] rational ansatz family. The Pade restriction is itself an ansatz, not a derived constraint.
The Newtonian and deep-MOND boundary conditions are imported from Milgrom (1983) and Bekenstein-Milgrom (1984).
claims.limitations: Does not establish that MOND emerges independently of MOND assumptions; the boundary conditions that fix the form are the definition of MOND.

claims.wording: Fisher identity: F'_dual(x)^2 * I(mu(x)) = x^3, with odds-ratio inverse mu(odds(p)) = p.
assumptions: I(mu) = 1/(mu(1-mu)) is the Bernoulli Fisher information, used as an algebraic definition.
claims.limitations: An algebraic identity over the reals. It does NOT derive galactic gravity from a statistical estimation process or from a minimum-Fisher-information variational principle.

claims.wording: Legendre dual: p = x^2/(1+x), x(p) = (p + sqrt(p^2+4p))/2, H_dual(p) = p x(p) - F(x(p)) strictly convex with H'' = 1/F''.
assumptions: F is strictly convex on the domain, so the Legendre transform is well defined.
claims.limitations: Establishes the transform and its convexity. No physical interpretation of the conjugate momentum is established here.

claims.wording: RETRACTED: the anti-drift gate 'u >= gamma <=> chi >= theta' is false. The GKSL steady-state coherence C(x) = 4x/(1+8x^2) is non-monotonic, peaking at theta = 1/sqrt(2) at u/gamma = theta/2 and decaying thereafter, whereas mu(x) = x/sqrt(1+x^2) rises monotonically. theta is a ceiling on coherence, not a threshold gate. The identification of the steady-state coherence with mu(u/gamma) does not hold.
assumptions: The driven damped two-level system is modelled by the standard GKSL generator with a single sigma_minus jump operator.
The coherence observable is the equatorial Bloch component of the analytic steady state.
claims.limitations: The ceiling C_max = theta is a standard optical-Bloch result. What remains a framework claim, and is not established here, is the identification of that maximum with the sovereign band constant theta. The Uhlmann fidelity statement 'F >= 1/2 <=> chi >= 1/sqrt(2)' is still open and is not formalized.

claims.wording: Pillar IV: the GKSL generator on Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) C has the stated analytical steady state with unit trace; mu(1) = 1/sqrt2; and the two-channel union is strictly monotone on [0,1], supporting a gate-type iff.
assumptions: The GKSL generator, jump operator and drive Hamiltonian are as constructed in the module.
claims.limitations: 16 theorems close on [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] only, and perturbing the constants (mu 1 -> mu 2, kappaBand 7/10 -> 8/10, 1/(2 sqrt2) -> 1/(3 sqrt2)) breaks the proofs, so the values are derived rather than assumed. The earlier anti-drift gate u >= gamma <=> chi >= theta is FALSE and retracted: the steady-state coherence is non-monotonic. Nothing here certifies that the modelled generator describes a physical system.
